acceptance.accepted_history_rule: Only the event exactly anchored by CURRENT.latest_event commit+path+digest is accepted history.
acceptance.canonicalization_gate: Reject repeated JSON object member names before semantic parsing, canonicalization, idempotency derivation, or event hashing.
acceptance.duplicate_rule: Existing deterministic claim path is DUPLICATE; do not replace claim, outbox, event, or CURRENT.
acceptance.pointer_gate: Fetch CURRENT again; it must remain exact v72/blob b5a53b2a1abbc4f193b67b26c9d8f11ddb7f4e12/stored projection digest 8b2dec9b613f73cad89ddac931526c7ae031a4009db1d2fe7519fd76d94070d6 before one blob-SHA-guarded replacement; final readback must be v73.
acceptance.slack_gate: Slack post is prohibited before exact v73 readback anchors this event commit+path+digest; then post one sanitized exact-marker pointer and append one immutable delivery receipt.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This is one local Python parser and one strict object-pairs hook, not a cross-language or standards conformance test. The controlled specimen exercises one top-level repeated member only; nested duplicates, escaped-equivalent member names, parser streaming behavior, and other implementations remain untested. The strict gate demonstrates fail-closed behavior in this wake but does not prove every future producer applies it before hashing. Claim, outbox, event, CURRENT replacement, Slack post, and delivery receipt are separate effects. Git supplies branch-local create-only paths and a single-file prior-blob-SHA replacement precondition only; it provides no cross-file transaction, database uniqueness or isolation, linearizability, exactly-once execution, force-push safety, cross-branch exclusion, or Slack atomicity.

probe.name: JSON_DUPLICATE_OBJECT_MEMBER_REJECTION_V1

operation_payload.controlled_factor: Vary only whether the raw JSON object contains a repeated member name. Keep the effective last-wins value, all other members, UTF-8 encoding, restricted integer values, canonical serializer, object version chain, and write protocol fixed.
operation_payload.hypothesis: A strict canonicalization ingress must reject repeated object member names before semantic parsing or hashing; otherwise distinct raw bytes can silently collapse to one parsed object under a last-wins parser.

measured_result.result: The ordinary local parser used last-wins behavior and collapsed the duplicate-member specimen onto the unique control. The strict pairs hook rejected the duplicate before canonicalization. C19 wake 1 therefore records duplicate-member rejection as a required fail-closed ingress gate, not as proof of cross-language conformance.

native_task_read.title: HFO X12 Durable Object PDCA Lab

operation_payload.result_contract: Record local parser behavior exactly; require duplicate-member rejection before canonicalization; do not claim RFC conformance, parser independence, or database uniqueness.

probe.strongest_falsifier: A strict replay accepts the repeated member, the ordinary parser does not collapse the two specimens as recorded, raw or canonical digests recompute differently, the deterministic claim already existed but state still advances, CURRENT is not exact v72 on the second read, or final event/CURRENT binding fails.

canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete the claim, outbox, event, Slack message, or receipt. If v73 is later invalid, append a compensating transition from the then-current exact version. Correct duplicate-key policy only through a later versioned event.
